U.S. Customs and Border Protection posted an estimated 80-minute wait for standard passenger vehicles alongside a 5-minute wait for standard commercial vehicles at the Brownsville Veterans International port of entry (port 535502) at 6:00 p.m. CST on Nov. 11, 2026 [S-1000082].

According to the agency's port feed, one of eight maximum passenger vehicle lanes was open for standard manual processing with an 80-minute delay, two Ready Lanes were open with an 80-minute delay, and two NEXUS/SENTRI lanes were open with a 30-minute delay [S-1000082].

On the freight side, two of four maximum commercial vehicle lanes were open under RFID processing with a 5-minute wait and no reported delay, while FAST lanes were listed as closed [S-1000082].

Standard pedestrian processing had one of two maximum lanes open with zero minutes of delay, and Ready Lanes for pedestrians were listed as not applicable; the crossing operates from 6 a.m. to midnight and reported open status with no construction notice [S-1000082].
deck: A U.S. Customs and Border Protection feed posted a 75-minute gap between passenger and commercial vehicle wait times at the Veterans International crossing in Brownsville on Nov. 11, 2026.
headline: Brownsville Border Crossing Sees Estimated Wait Times of Up to 80 Minutes for Passenger Vehicles
uncertainty_disclosures: U.S. Customs and Border Protection posted wait times are point-in-time estimates; the sealed source does not show whether delays persisted across later updates.
The port feed lists open lane counts and closed FAST lanes but does not explain staffing levels or why additional passenger lanes were closed.
The sealed source contains no information on commercial cargo volumes, specific commuter delays, or downstream traffic impacts.

verified_claims.claim: Port 535502 (Brownsville, Veterans International) reported a 5-minute wait for standard commercial lanes (2 of 4 lanes open, RFID) at 6:00 p.m. CST on 11/11/2026.

Standard passenger lanes (1 of 8 lanes open, Manual) and passenger Ready Lanes (2 lanes open) each reported an 80-minute delay at 6:00 p.m. CST on 11/11/2026, while NEXUS/SENTRI lanes (2 open) reported a 30-minute delay.
Commercial FAST lanes were listed as closed, and standard pedestrian processing (1 of 2 lanes open) reported a 0-minute wait.

A Washington Public Disclosure Commission record lists a $300.00 cash contribution received on November 5, 2026, by the Snohomish County Democratic Party (Campaign - Non-Exempt), which the record classifies as a political committee, for the 2026 election year. [S-1000043]

The record lists the contributor's category as an organization based in Washington, gives the jurisdiction as Various, and includes no description of the contribution. [S-1000043]

The receipt is filed under report number 110402358 by the committee with filer ID SNOHDCN206. [S-1000043]
deck: A Washington Public Disclosure Commission record lists one cash receipt for the 2026 election year.
headline: Snohomish County Democratic Party committee reports $300 cash contribution from Washington organization
uncertainty_disclosures: The triage lead names the contributor, but the fields selected in the sealed source do not include a contributor name, so this draft does not identify the contributor. Re-fetching the record with the contributor_name field would be needed to verify it.
The record lists for_or_against as against, and the source does not explain what that field means for a party committee's receipt.
The anomaly statistics in the triage lead are not in the sealed source, so this draft makes no claim that the contribution is unusual.
No officials or seats are identified in the sealed source.
The sealed source supports only a single routine contribution record. It does not on its own support a larger story.

verified_claims.claim: The Snohomish County Democratic Party (Campaign - Non-Exempt) reported receiving a $300.00 cash contribution on November 5, 2026.
The record classifies the filer as a political committee and lists election year 2026.
The contributor is categorized as an organization located in Washington.
The record lists jurisdiction as Various and contains no description of the contribution.
The receipt appears in report number 110402358 filed under filer ID SNOHDCN206.
